topics.label: DJI AGRAS T25
topics.description: The January 2025 v1.0 manual specifies a 20 L spraying tank and 20 kg operating spray payload for T25. Aircraft mass including battery is 32 kg and sea-level maximum takeoff mass for spraying is 52 kg. Strong-GNSS D-RTK hover accuracy is ±10 cm horizontally and vertically. Its atomizing spray system is not a demonstrated funnel-filling attachment; no current price, regional availability or operational permission is implied. The same manual reports reference hover times of 14.5 minutes without spray payload and 7 minutes at full spray load, with a 15.5 Ah battery. These are reference hover tests, not maximum forward-flight or reservoir-servicing mission durations.

topics.description: Manufacturer specifications captured on 10 November 2026 distinguish configurations: the standard LS100 spraying system lists a 100 L tank and 100 kg operating payload; LS100-DB dual battery retains a 100 L tank but lists 90 kg operating payload. topics.label: DJI Mavic 2 Pro (standard aircraft)
topics.description: The standard DJI Mavic 2 Pro airframe is separate from the school-garden watering assembly. DJI’s July 2020 v2.2 manual lists a 907 g takeoff weight, a maximum flight time of 31 minutes at a consistent 25 km/h without wind, and a maximum hover time of 29 minutes without wind. It separately gives an overall flight time of 25 minutes in normal flight with 15% battery remaining. That last value is a manufacturer reference, not a mission estimate calculated for this project. The standard flight battery is 3850 mAh, 15.4 V and 59.29 Wh. None of these reference times establishes endurance with the added pump, reservoir, auxiliary battery and water. The reviewed manual does not establish a rated watering payload; the prototype’s short loaded tests do not supply one.

topics.label: Mavic 2 Pro water-payload prototype
topics.description: The UAE preliminary study used a DJI Mavic 2 Pro with a removable approximately 400 g dry pump/reservoir/control assembly and test water loads of 250, 500 and 750 mL. A ground probe and wireless control switched the pump against an uncalibrated relative moisture index. These reported experimental loads are not a manufacturer payload rating or an approved configuration; the paper itself calls for a rated airframe and mass/load assessment before routine use. The nine loaded flights lasted 2:18–3:54 and the six integrated flights 2:47–3:52. These were completed short tests, not endurance-to-exhaustion measurements. Standard-aircraft manufacturer figures remain on the separate Mavic 2 Pro record.

topics.label: Study: Dubai individual-plant drone watering prototype (2026)
topics.description: Antony Sheshenya’s Dubai American Academy study built a removable pump and tank for a Mavic 2 Pro and a wireless soil-probe link, tested around six potted basil plants in a covered courtyard. Eight bench runs measured pump flow, followed by ground tests, nine loaded flights and six integrated sensor-controlled flights. Loaded test flights lasted 2:18–3:54 and integrated flights 2:47–3:52, without testing maximum endurance. The aircraft was manually piloted; the pump used an uncalibrated relative moisture index with hysteresis. Integrated-flight water quantities were estimated from bench flow multiplied by pump-on time, not collected at the plant. The study demonstrates preliminary payload/control feasibility but did not measure targeting accuracy, root-zone capture fraction, routine safe payload, useful endurance or plant benefit. It calls for a rated airframe and further testing. Publisher HTML is dated 3 November 2026, while the PDF lists electronic access on 15 November 2026; that unresolved date discrepancy is preserved. No autonomous flight or reservoir-filling result is established.

topics.label: Proposed drone-refilled seedling reservoir
topics.description: User proposal from the 10 November 2026 chat: plant nursery stock together with a tube or local reservoir, then have a drone visit and refill it. The suggested 0.5 L every couple of days is an assumed design scenario; species, soil, climate, stock size and exact interval are unspecified. Reviewed sources establish separate components: buried pipe/sleeve delivery, passive reservoirs, small manually piloted water-payload tests, an indoor funnel invention, and larger agricultural spray aircraft. Their combination has not been validated in the reviewed evidence. A fill opening, transferred-volume measurement, overflow/loss control and a suitable soil outlet must work together. As a capacity-only calculation, 40 L divided by an assumed 0.5 L gives 80 fills before reserves, losses, travel and time constraints; it is not measured plants per flight or per hour. Component citations support this curated concept, not the assumed dose or an empirical system outcome. A separate illustrative calculation deducts an assumed 20% time allowance from full-load reference hover durations; it is not a flight itinerary, a battery reserve rule or a validated mission estimate.
